1: [[espn:662|Paul Pierce]] and [[espn:110|Kobe Bryant]] traded big scoring nights, but Boston escaped Staples Center with a 112–111 victory. Pierce finished with 39 points, seven rebounds and four assists, while Bryant led all scorers with 40 points, eight rebounds and six assists. The one-point finish gave your first NBA game a memorable ending between two of the league’s oldest rivals.

The Lakers led 58–54 at halftime before Boston outscored them 37–24 in the third quarter, taking a 91–82 advantage into the fourth. [[espn:2422|Delonte West]] supplied 19 points and 10 assists, and [[espn:2757|Ryan Gomes]] added 19 points and 12 rebounds on 8-of-10 shooting. [[espn:831|Wally Szczerbiak]] contributed 16 points as the Celtics built enough offense around Pierce to withstand a late Los Angeles rally.

The finish remained in doubt until the final shot. A Gomes tip-in put Boston ahead 110–106 with 56.7 seconds left, but [[espn:617|Lamar Odom]] completed a three-point play to tie the game at 111 with 15.3 seconds remaining. Pierce then drew a foul from Bryant and made the first of two free throws with 3.2 seconds left. He missed the second, giving the Lakers one last chance, but Bryant’s attempt from the top of the key missed at the buzzer. Boston survived despite scoring only 21 points in the fourth quarter.
2: [[espn:110|Kobe Bryant]] powered the Los Angeles Lakers to a 109–89 win over the Phoenix Suns at Staples Center, scoring 43 points with eight rebounds and five assists. The Lakers seized control early, opening with a 35–22 first quarter and extending the margin to 62–41 at halftime. Bryant did much of his damage at the foul line, converting 20 of 23 free throws.

Phoenix had its own standout performances: [[espn:510|Shawn Marion]] scored 29 points and grabbed seven rebounds, while [[espn:2167|Boris Diaw]] assembled an 11-point, 10-rebound, 12-assist triple-double. [[espn:2166|Leandro Barbosa]] added 16 points, but the Suns could not erase the early deficit. Phoenix won the third quarter 29–21, trimming the lead to 13 entering the fourth.

The Lakers answered with a 26–19 final period to complete the 20-point victory. [[espn:617|Lamar Odom]] contributed 14 points, 11 rebounds and seven assists, [[espn:1823|Smush Parker]] added 12 points and eight rebounds, and [[espn:2027|Luke Walton]] collected eight points, 10 rebounds and six assists. Los Angeles finished the regular-season home matchup with an emphatic win over a Phoenix team it would soon face in the playoffs.
3: The Los Angeles Lakers ground out an 82–72 win over the Chicago Bulls at Staples Center in a defensive, low-scoring contest. Chicago led 21–19 after the first quarter, but the Lakers moved ahead 38–35 at halftime. [[espn:617|Lamar Odom]] paced Los Angeles with 23 points, 10 rebounds and four assists, while [[espn:110|Kobe Bryant]] scored 18 points with four rebounds and four assists.

[[espn:2456|Andres Nocioni]] carried Chicago's offense, scoring a game-high 30 points and hitting six of nine three-pointers. [[espn:2429|Luol Deng]] added 13 points, and [[espn:885|Ben Wallace]] collected eight points and 12 rebounds. The Bulls stayed within three points entering the final period, trailing 62–59, but struggled to find offense down the stretch.

The Lakers held Chicago to 13 fourth-quarter points and finished with a 20–13 edge in the period. [[espn:2748|Andrew Bynum]] supplied 12 points, 13 rebounds and four blocked shots, helping Los Angeles win the rebounding battle 51–42. The Bulls shot just 27-for-80 from the field, while the Lakers survived 22 turnovers to secure their ten-point victory. Bryant's late free throws and an Odom dunk in the closing seconds put the result beyond reach.
4: The Clippers broke open a close game with a 34-point third quarter and defeated Sacramento 102–93 at Staples Center. Los Angeles held a narrow 46–45 halftime lead before outscoring the Kings 34–24 in the third, turning a one-point edge into an 80–69 advantage. [[espn:91|Elton Brand]] led the Clippers with 22 points and three blocks, while [[espn:497|Corey Maggette]] scored 21 off the bench.

[[espn:566|Cuttino Mobley]] added 17 points and six rebounds, and [[espn:1982|Chris Kaman]] supplied 14 points, eight rebounds and three blocks. [[espn:2393|Shaun Livingston]] directed the offense with five assists. Sacramento got a game-high 26 points from [[espn:61|Mike Bibby]], along with 15 points and five assists from [[espn:556|Brad Miller]], but could not erase the deficit after the Clippers' decisive third period.

The win gave Los Angeles a 13–16 record and reversed its 93–80 defeat in Sacramento a month earlier. The Clippers' balanced scoring complemented Brand's interior presence, while the Kings fell to 12–15 despite Bibby's scoring performance.
5: [[espn:91|Elton Brand]] dominated both ends of the floor with 32 points and eight blocked shots, leading the Clippers to a 90–80 New Year's Eve victory over the New York Knicks at Staples Center. Brand shot 13-for-18 from the field, tied his career high in blocks, and anchored a defense that limited New York to 38 first-half points.

Los Angeles built a 51–38 halftime advantage and extended it to 74–55 after three quarters. [[espn:2393|Shaun Livingston]] contributed 15 points and seven assists, while [[espn:1982|Chris Kaman]] collected 13 rebounds. The Knicks got 15 points from [[espn:990|Eddy Curry]], 14 points and eight assists from [[espn:509|Stephon Marbury]], and 12 points from [[espn:2754|Channing Frye]].

New York outscored the Clippers 25–16 in the final quarter but never overcame the earlier deficit. The win was Los Angeles' fourth in five games after a six-game losing streak, with Brand's eight-block performance standing out as the defining individual achievement.
6: The Clippers beat Charlotte 100–93 at Staples Center, but the night was overshadowed by a devastating first-quarter injury to [[espn:2393|Shaun Livingston]]. Driving for a fast-break layup, the young point guard landed awkwardly and collapsed with a serious left-knee injury. He was taken from the court with 8:10 remaining in the opening quarter, leaving Los Angeles to regroup without him.

[[espn:497|Corey Maggette]] led the Clippers with a season-high 25 points despite making only three field goals, going 19-for-20 at the free-throw line. [[espn:91|Elton Brand]] contributed 14 points and 12 rebounds, while [[espn:566|Cuttino Mobley]] scored 16 and [[espn:138|Sam Cassell]] added 14. Los Angeles held on for the seven-point win in a game whose result became secondary to concern for its injured guard.

[[espn:1026|Gerald Wallace]] paced the Bobcats with 20 points and 12 rebounds, [[espn:2211|Matt Carroll]] added 19 points and nine boards, and rookie [[espn:3016|Adam Morrison]] scored 15. Charlotte was without injured big man Emeka Okafor. Subsequent medical evaluation revealed extensive ligament and cartilage damage to Livingston's knee, making this one of the most consequential and sobering games in the Clippers' season.
7: [[espn:110|Kobe Bryant]] followed his 65-point explosion against Portland with 50 more in a 109–102 Lakers victory over Minnesota at Staples Center. Bryant shot 17-for-35 from the field, hit four three-pointers and made 12 of 14 free throws, becoming the first Laker since Elgin Baylor in 1962 to score at least 50 in consecutive games. He attacked early, scoring 14 points in the opening eight-plus minutes as Los Angeles established control.

The Lakers led 52–43 at halftime and broke the game open with a 35-point third quarter. Bryant scored 16 in the period, including a three-pointer at the buzzer that stretched the advantage to 87–68. [[espn:1823|Smush Parker]] provided 19 points, seven rebounds and nine assists, while [[espn:617|Lamar Odom]] added 16 points, nine rebounds and eight assists. [[espn:2027|Luke Walton]] contributed 10 points and 11 assists.

Minnesota made the finish uncomfortable, rallying behind [[espn:193|Ricky Davis]], who scored 33 points, and [[espn:261|Kevin Garnett]], who had 26 points and 15 rebounds. Davis' late three-pointer trimmed the deficit to 95–92 with 2:55 left, but Bryant answered with a critical three-point play and later punctuated the win with a fast-break dunk. The Lakers survived the fourth-quarter surge and Bryant's remarkable two-game scoring total reached 115 points.
8: Phoenix held off Los Angeles 115–107 at Staples Center, riding a 41-point fourth quarter to defeat the Lakers. [[espn:592|Steve Nash]] led the Suns with 25 points and 11 assists, while [[espn:2166|Leandro Barbosa]] supplied 23 points and [[espn:49|Raja Bell]] added 22, making all six of his three-point attempts. Phoenix led 54–48 at halftime, but the Lakers cut the gap to a single point entering the final period.

[[espn:110|Kobe Bryant]] scored 34 points and handed out seven assists for Los Angeles, shooting 14-for-25. [[espn:1823|Smush Parker]] matched 25 points with six assists, while [[espn:2789|Ronny Turiaf]] contributed 19 points and 15 rebounds on 8-for-10 shooting. The Lakers held a 51–40 rebounding edge, but their 17 turnovers and 14-for-21 free-throw shooting hurt their chances.

The Suns' closing surge secured the eight-point win despite Los Angeles scoring 34 in the fourth. [[espn:1727|Amar'e Stoudemire]] finished with 19 points and nine rebounds, and Phoenix went 29-for-34 at the foul line. The result offered another chapter in a Western Conference rivalry that would continue into the postseason.
9: Sacramento held off a furious Clippers comeback to win 105–100 at Staples Center. The Kings jumped ahead 34–23 in the first quarter and carried a 60–41 lead into halftime, putting Los Angeles in a deep hole. [[espn:2755|Francisco Garcia]] scored a team-high 16 points, while [[espn:61|Mike Bibby]] and [[espn:25|Metta World Peace]] each had 15; World Peace also handed out 10 assists.

The Clippers fought back behind [[espn:91|Elton Brand]], who delivered 29 points, 14 rebounds and seven assists. [[espn:497|Corey Maggette]] added 21 points and 10 rebounds, and [[espn:2188|Quinton Ross]] scored 14. Los Angeles outscored Sacramento 35–24 in the fourth quarter, turning a 16-point deficit after three periods into a close finish.

Sacramento's early advantage ultimately held up. [[espn:2394|Kevin Martin]] scored 13 points, as did [[espn:1726|John Salmons]], and the Kings distributed the scoring across their rotation. The Clippers had a final opportunity to narrow the five-point margin, but Maggette missed a three-pointer in the closing seconds, leaving Sacramento with the road victory.
10: Phoenix shook off a slow start to beat the Los Angeles Clippers 113–94 at US Airways Center. The Clippers led 27–22 after one quarter and held a 52–51 halftime edge, but the Suns took control with a 35–22 third period. [[espn:1727|Amar'e Stoudemire]] scored 29 points on 10-of-16 shooting and grabbed 11 rebounds, leading Phoenix's inside attack.

[[espn:510|Shawn Marion]] contributed 21 points and 17 rebounds, while [[espn:592|Steve Nash]] paired 20 points with 10 assists. [[espn:336|Grant Hill]] added 19 points as Phoenix outscored Los Angeles 62–42 after halftime and improved to 11–2.

[[espn:138|Sam Cassell]] led the Clippers with 26 points, [[espn:638|Ruben Patterson]] had 18 points and 11 rebounds, and [[espn:1982|Chris Kaman]] posted 17 points and 14 rebounds. Los Angeles could not keep pace after the break, finishing with just 20 fourth-quarter points.
11: San Antonio edged the Los Angeles Clippers 88–82 at Staples Center behind 26 points from [[espn:1015|Tony Parker]] and a strong finish from [[espn:272|Manu Ginobili]]. The Clippers led 24–21 after the first quarter and stretched their advantage to 37–27 in the second, but the Spurs rallied to tie the game 42–42 at halftime.

[[espn:215|Tim Duncan]] supplied 17 points and 17 rebounds, helping San Antonio recover from its early deficit. The teams traded leads in the third quarter before Ginobili's free throws put the Spurs ahead 64–62 entering the fourth. Playing his first game back after missing five with a sprained finger, Ginobili scored 12 of his 23 points in the final period.

[[espn:1982|Chris Kaman]] led Los Angeles with 20 points and 14 rebounds, while rookie [[espn:3237|Al Thornton]] added 17 points and eight boards and [[espn:497|Corey Maggette]] scored 14. The Clippers kept the game close, but San Antonio's 25 made free throws on 36 attempts, compared with eight makes on 12 attempts for Los Angeles, helped decide the six-point result.
12: Utah controlled the middle quarters at Staples Center, turning a 23–20 first-quarter edge into a 54–43 halftime lead and pulling away for a 109–93 win over the Clippers. [[espn:2798|Deron Williams]] directed the Jazz offense with 18 points and 13 assists, shooting 8-for-14 from the floor, as Utah steadily expanded its advantage.

The Jazz received a balanced contribution from their bench: [[espn:3015|Paul Millsap]] and [[espn:306|Matt Harpring]] each scored 17 points, and [[espn:2011|Kyle Korver]] added 13, including three three-pointers. [[espn:1703|Carlos Boozer]] finished with 12 points and 12 rebounds, while [[espn:2991|Ronnie Brewer]] scored 15.

[[espn:497|Corey Maggette]] paced Los Angeles with 23 points and six rebounds, while [[espn:1982|Chris Kaman]] supplied 17 points and 10 rebounds. The Clippers never recovered from Utah's 31–23 second quarter, and the Jazz won the fourth 30–26 to finish with a 16-point margin.
13: In a marquee meeting of two of the NBA's biggest stars, [[espn:1966|LeBron James]] scored 41 points and led Cleveland to a 98–95 road win over the Lakers. [[espn:110|Kobe Bryant]] answered with 33 points, 12 rebounds and six assists, but James scored 14 in the fourth quarter as the Cavaliers prevailed in a game that featured 21 lead changes and nine ties. A small roof leak even interrupted play for about 12 minutes in the first quarter.

Cleveland led 49–40 at halftime before Los Angeles surged in the third quarter and briefly built a nine-point lead in the fourth. The Cavaliers rallied, and James put Cleveland ahead 94–93 with a basket inside the final 90 seconds. He then hit a jumper with about 20 seconds remaining to stretch the lead to three. After [[espn:2789|Ronny Turiaf]] scored on a putback, James made two free throws, and the Lakers failed to release a final three-point attempt before the buzzer.

James shot 16-for-32, grabbed nine rebounds and handed out four assists. [[espn:362|Zydrunas Ilgauskas]] supplied 16 points and 11 rebounds, while [[espn:356|Larry Hughes]] added 16 points for Cleveland. [[espn:617|Lamar Odom]] finished with 14 points and nine rebounds for the Lakers, who were playing without injured center Andrew Bynum. The showdown ended with James winning the individual scoring duel and Cleveland taking the three-point victory.
31: [[espn:110|Kobe Bryant]] took over after halftime as the Los Angeles Lakers beat the Houston Rockets 104–88 at Staples Center. Houston led 52–51 at the break behind [[espn:1722|Yao Ming]], who had already collected 20 points and 10 rebounds. Bryant had 19 first-half points, setting up a duel between the two stars.

The third quarter decided the game. Bryant scored 22 points in the period, hitting nine of 13 shots, as Los Angeles outscored Houston 37–18 and turned a one-point halftime deficit into an 88–70 advantage. He finished with 43 points on 19-of-32 shooting, including three three-pointers, along with six assists. The Rockets never seriously threatened the lead in the final quarter.

Yao finished with 33 points and 16 rebounds on 16-of-25 shooting, but Houston received little scoring support beyond [[espn:11|Rafer Alston]]'s 12 points and six assists. [[espn:617|Lamar Odom]] added 21 points and six rebounds for the Lakers, while [[espn:1823|Smush Parker]] supplied 15 points and 10 assists. The decisive third-quarter burst overshadowed Yao's impressive performance.
